controls.prompt: four floors, 7 bays, brick, flat roof, ornate trim

references.observation: Three levels and four upper front bays. Use masonry, opening depth and crown hierarchy; the canonical four-floor seven-bay building is not a proportional replica.
Four levels including the contrasting red base. Use base/body distinction, without adopting all facade ornament.

criteria.label: Massing and base
criteria.criterion: Base, body and crown read immediately; commercial base differs from upper floors; roof does not bury the crown and shadows support the form.

criteria.label: Facade rhythm
criteria.criterion: Openings align and piers read as masonry; hierarchy avoids an equally heavy grid. Raking light reveals no clipping or misaligned joins.

criteria.label: Opening depth and glazing
criteria.criterion: Returns, frames and glass remain separate; glazing differs visibly from solid trim, and all facade glass faces outward correctly.

criteria.label: Trim layering and restraint
criteria.criterion: A dominant crown has subordinate belts and window trim; ledges do not overwhelm the wall. Layers cast coherent shadows without floating or flicker.

criteria.label: Material scale and roles
criteria.criterion: Wall brick courses use the existing 75 mm anchor; role/channel orientation is correct. One- and four-metre swatches have equal physical density, without sampling neighbouring slots.

criteria.label: Side and rear coherence
criteria.criterion: Simpler elevations, corner and cornice returns and ground contact form competent generated architecture. No fidelity claim is made for reference elevations not shown.
